body: A few measurement-level concerns. (1) The spec's temporal-alignment requirement is not established by the data sources it names: ACE SWICS composition products are typically 2-hour cadence (and have documented degradation/gaps, especially after ~2011 and during SWICS/SWICS-2 transitions), so 'exactly one row per hour' with 'no missing values' for composition-derived ratios is unlikely to be achievable; the edge-case clause about gaps exceeding 6 hours does not cover the more common case of chronic low-cadence coverage. (2) Kp is published at 3-hour resolution, not hourly; the assumption that it 'can be reliably interpolated to hourly' is asserted, not demonstrated, and hourly interpolation of Kp would manufacture autocorrelated values that inflate the apparent sample size for significance tests. (3) The 5-fold cross-validation is specified without blocking or temporal ordering; with strongly autocorrelated hourly data over 20 years, random folds will leak information across train/test boundaries, so the 'out-of-sample R²' in FR-007 would not measure out-of-sample gain. The permutation test is blocked (24-hour blocks), but the CV is not — the two standards are inconsistent. (4) SC-001 conflates two distinct claims: a permutation p<0.05 establishes statistical significance, while the ΔR²>0.05 'practical' threshold is an arbitrary constant with no stated justification. (5) The parent methodology says 'nearest-neighbor interpolation' while this spec mandates 'hourly median aggregation' — an unresolved contradiction in how the unified dataset is to be produced.
